seoDescription: Learn how to connect one NestJS application to another using WebSockets in this detailed tutorial. Building on a previously created WebSocket server, you'll see how to create a separate NestJS consumer application that acts as a WebSocket client. This guide covers using the `socket.io-client` library to establish a server-to-server connection, enabling your backend services to consume live data. You will learn to emit events from the client and handle incoming events from the WebSocket gateway, a crucial pattern for real-time systems.

chapters.title: Introduction & Project Setup
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the goal of connecting a new NestJS application as a client to an existing NestJS WebSocket server.

chapters.title: Creating the Socket Module
chapters.description: This chapter covers creating a dedicated module for socket functionality and explains the role of the `socket.io-client` library.

chapters.title: Implementing the Socket Client Service
chapters.description: This chapter walks through creating an injectable `SocketClient` service and adding it to the module's providers.

chapters.title: Installing Dependencies & Establishing the Connection
chapters.description: This chapter details installing the `socket.io-client` dependency and writing the code to initialize the connection to the WebSocket server.

chapters.title: Listening for the Connection Event
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates using the `OnModuleInit` lifecycle hook to safely listen for the 'connect' event and confirm the connection is established.

chapters.title: Testing the Connection and Fixing Port Conflicts
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to run the client application, diagnose and fix a port conflict, and verify a successful connection with the server.

chapters.title: Consuming Events from the WebSocket Server
chapters.description: This chapter explains how to register a listener for the custom `onMessage` event being emitted by the WebSocket server.

chapters.title: Emitting Events and Tracing the Round-Trip Flow
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates emitting a `newMessage` event from the client to the server and traces the full communication cycle back to the client.

chapters.title: Verifying Broadcast with a Second Client (Postman)
chapters.description: This chapter uses Postman to act as a second client, proving that the server broadcasts messages to all connected clients, including the NestJS consumer.

chapters.title: Conclusion & Next Steps
chapters.description: This chapter summarizes the server-to-server WebSocket communication pattern and previews the next tutorial on connecting a React front-end client.

## Consuming Events from the WebSocket Server

So let's go into our consumer project and let's actually consume those events that are being sent from the websocket server. Okay, so we have the consumer, which is going to consume those events, and then we have the emitter. I'll call the emitter. The emitter is going to emit the events, so that's the websocket gateway. Okay, so this way it'll register all the events once the socket.io client has been initialized, otherwise if you call it before it's been initialized, it's going to give you a null error.

Okay so what we'll do now is we'll just simply register all of our events down here. So `this.socketClient.on('onMessage')`. Okay? So we're going to basically trigger the `newMessage` event right over here. So watch this.
